result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): B has a clearer desk flow: one member lookup field that accepts an ID or name, a lend/return toggle, multi-tool add with an empty-state hint, a filter on loans that are out, and a Clear button. It also uses terms more consistently (member, tool, due back), though 'check out' still appears beside 'lend'. However, B states an invented 7-day lending period (up to 14) as fact and shows inventory totals. A also shows totals and an unlabeled default return date, makes the volunteer type member details with no lookup, and mixes 'return by', 'due', 'borrowed by' and 'check in'. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): A wins narrowly: it has a clear Lend/Return toggle, a member lookup field, a list of tools that are out with one-click Return, and it mostly keeps the same words (member, tool, due back). However, it states a made-up policy as fact ('Lending period is 7 days (up to 14)') and shows inventory totals. B has lending and returning side by side, which works well, but it mixes its terms (lend, take back, check in, return by, due, borrowed by), has no member lookup, and also shows invented inventory counts. Neither screenshot shows messages for member not found, a tool already out, or nothing lent, and neither labels its preset due date as a default.
